stem: A form field has a visible error message below it. Which markup best ensures a screen reader announces the error when the field receives focus?

options.text: Use `aria-describedby` to associate the input with the error.
options.rationale: aria-describedby points to the error text, so the field's description includes the message when it receives focus.

options.text: Use `title` on the input to repeat the visible error message.
options.rationale: A title may be exposed as a description, but it is not tied to the visible error and support is inconsistent.

options.text: Use `placeholder` on the input to repeat the visible error message.
options.rationale: A placeholder is not an error message and disappears once the user starts typing.

options.text: Place the error text beside the input so everyone can see it.
options.rationale: Visible text is not announced with the field unless it is programmatically associated with it.

explanation: An error message must be programmatically associated with the field it describes. `aria-describedby` referencing the message's `id` adds it to the field's accessible description, so screen reader users hear it when they reach the field. A nearby paragraph, placeholder, or title does not create that association reliably.

references.title: W3C WAI — Forms Tutorial: User Notifications
